subject.title: Feature Request: Automated Session Memory Preservation & Synthesis

question: Should automatic session-memory synthesis and transcript linking be a bundled core hook behavior, a memory-plugin capability, or a ClawHub/plugin package built on existing hook and memory APIs?
rationale: The code gap is real, but the permanent shape affects transcript retention, provider-backed summarization, storage format, startup context, memory-plugin ownership, and security defaults that automation should not choose.

options.title: Scope as memory-plugin/core contract
options.body: Define the minimum hook or memory-plugin API needed for synthesis and transcript-linking, then implement the chosen default with explicit privacy and retention rules.

options.title: Keep as bundled hook enhancement
options.body: Add opt-in synthesis and linking directly to the bundled session-memory hook, accepting the added config and privacy surface in core.

options.title: Route to ClawHub/plugin package
options.body: Leave core unchanged and ask contributors to publish a plugin or MCP package using existing hook and memory surfaces unless a missing API is proven.

recommendation.title: Scope as memory-plugin/core contract
recommendation.body: Define the minimum hook or memory-plugin API needed for synthesis and transcript-linking, then implement the chosen default with explicit privacy and retention rules.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest current source-history signal on the session-memory hook and recent sanitizer work.
